read_first.q: How do I do robotics and AI inside ECE?
read_first.a: Already published. ECE's own course guide lists 18-461 Introduction to Machine Learning for Engineers, 18-395 Introduction to Computer Vision, 18-370 Fundamentals of Control and 18-475 Autonomous Control Systems, and every ECE course numbered 18-300 or higher counts toward the Coverage requirement. On top of that the Robotics Additional Major is open to students in all colleges at a 3.0 GPA, and the Robotics Minor and Machine Learning Minor are reserved for students OUTSIDE the School of Computer Science — so being in ECE is exactly what qualifies you.
Published in the same ECE academic guide. Worth knowing separately: ECE students need a cumulative, College of Engineering and ECE QPA of at least 2.0 to graduate.

read_first.q: Can I take School of Computer Science courses if I'm in ECE?
read_first.a: Yes in principle, but CMU's academic regulations say registration priority goes to students registering for courses in their primary major. So the real issue is whether you get a seat, which is a question for the ECE department, not admissions.

ask.q: Two of your own pages seem to disagree and it changes my whole application. Your admissions site says engineering applicants "apply to and are admitted directly to a department/major unless choosing undecided", but the College of Engineering catalog says engineering students "do not select a major until the end of the first year". If I name Electrical and Computer Engineering on my application, am I committed to it, or do I still choose at the end of first year?
ask.why: This decides whether applying Early Decision naming ECE is a safe choice or a lock-in.

ask.q: Is applying to engineering as "undecided" looked at differently from naming Electrical and Computer Engineering? I would rather name ECE, but not if it costs me the ability to switch.
ask.why: Your site says only undecided admits get to choose freely among engineering majors in spring.

ask.q: Your catalog says I may apply to up to two colleges, but only in Regular Decision. If I apply Regular Decision, am I allowed to choose the College of Engineering and the School of Computer Science as my two — or do both choices have to sit inside one college?
ask.why: Whether that specific pairing is allowed is not published anywhere.

ask.q: If my first-choice college turns me down, does my second-choice college actually read my application, or has the decision already been made by then?
ask.why: Determines whether a second choice is real insurance or decoration.

ask.q: You publish a 20.6% Early Decision admit rate against 11.07% overall, but also say Early and Regular applicants are admitted at almost exactly the same rate. Is there an Early Decision rate for the College of Engineering specifically?
ask.why: Nothing is published by college, and this is the number that would justify applying ED.

ask.q: Your site says requests to change majors after first year "are not guaranteed to be approved". In practice, how often does someone admitted to ECE end up moving to another engineering department?
ask.why: Turns a policy sentence into an actual probability.

ask.q: I want to take 18-461 Machine Learning for Engineers, 18-395 Computer Vision and 18-475 Autonomous Control Systems. Do ECE students reliably get seats in those, or do they fill up?
ask.why: Registration priority follows your primary major, so these are the courses that must be reachable.

ask.q: The Robotics Additional Major says it is open to students in all colleges with a 3.0 GPA. Is there a limit on how many ECE students can actually do it, and does it add a semester?
ask.why: This is the main route into robotics from ECE, so its real capacity matters.

ask.q: The Machine Learning Minor is only open to students outside the School of Computer Science, so I would qualify from ECE. Can an ECE student realistically fit its prerequisites — 15-121 or 15-122, 15-151 or 21-127, and a probability course — alongside the ECE core?
ask.why: Being eligible is not the same as it fitting in a four-year schedule.

ask.q: ECE groups its courses into Hardware Systems, Software Systems and Signals and Systems. If robotics is what I care about, which of those am I effectively choosing?
ask.why: Tells you which ECE area to aim at before you arrive.

ask.q: Mechanical Engineering here publishes elective groups called Robotics and Automation and Autonomous Systems and Machine Learning. If I care about robots that move, is Mechanical a better home than ECE — and can I reach the same machine learning courses from there?
ask.why: Worth testing the alternative engineering door while you are on campus.

dont_ask.q: Does visiting or showing interest help my application?
dont_ask.because: CMU's Common Data Set marks level of applicant's interest, alumni relation and interviews all as Not considered. The visit is for your information only.

dont_ask.q: Can I send a portfolio of my robotics work?

read_first.q: Do I apply to a specific major?
read_first.a: Yes. You apply to a named major such as Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering, or to an intercollege combined major that pairs two fields.

read_first.q: Can I sit in on a class while I visit?
read_first.a: No — Northeastern does not offer class visits to prospective students.

ask.q: I would be applying to Electrical or Computer Engineering. You also offer combined majors that pair engineering with computer science. Is a combined major a harder admit than plain engineering — and can I move into one after I arrive, or does it have to be on the application?
ask.why: The combined majors are Northeastern's distinctive route into software plus hardware.

ask.q: Your Common Data Set lists level of applicant's interest as "Considered", but your admissions pages do not explain what that means. What actually counts — does today's visit get recorded, and do virtual sessions or emails count too?
ask.why: Northeastern is one of the few schools here where a visit may genuinely help, so it is worth knowing what registers.

ask.q: You offer Early Decision, a second Early Decision round and Early Action. If I apply Early Decision to engineering, does that change which majors I can be considered for?
ask.why: Northeastern has more application plans than any other school on the list.

ask.q: Co-op is the main reason I am looking at Northeastern. Are there co-ops in robotics or autonomy specifically, and which semester would my first one be — how long am I away from campus?
ask.why: Co-op is the differentiator; robotics-specific placements are the thing to verify.

ask.q: I could not find a named robotics track inside the Electrical or Computer Engineering degree. How much robotics coursework is actually available to me, and who teaches it?
ask.why: Unlike WPI, Northeastern has no dedicated robotics degree — so the depth needs checking.

ask.q: Does doing co-ops mean I graduate in five years rather than four, and what does that do to the total cost?
ask.why: Changes the cost comparison against every other school on the list.

read_first.q: Do I apply directly to Robotics Engineering?
read_first.a: No. There is one Common Application for all first-year students and you are prompted to declare your major near the end of B-Term in your first year. WPI's own robotics page says "Undecided? No problem."

read_first.q: Does WPI care that I visited?
read_first.a: Yes, and it is the only school on your list that says so in plain prose: "As part of an undergraduate application, WPI does look at demonstrated interest."

ask.q: You say WPI does look at demonstrated interest. Does attending today get recorded against my application, and is there anything else that counts that I should be doing between now and 1 November?
ask.why: This is the one campus where the answer can actually change an outcome.

ask.q: Because I declare my major near the end of B-Term rather than on the application, is Robotics Engineering ever full by the time students declare — or is it genuinely open to anyone who wants it?
ask.why: No capacity gate is published, which is unusual for a flagship robotics programme.

ask.q: You have Early Decision, Early Decision 2, Early Action 1 and Early Action 2. Given I am applying to several schools due 1 November, which of these actually helps me and which just commits me early?
ask.why: WPI has the most complicated set of plans of any school on the list.

ask.q: Robotics Engineering here is ABET-accredited as engineering, which most robotics degrees are not. Does that accreditation constrain the curriculum — how much room is left for artificial intelligence and machine learning courses?
ask.why: WPI's accreditation is a genuine advantage; the question is what it costs in flexibility.

ask.q: Courses here run in seven-week A and B terms. For something like control theory or machine learning, is seven weeks enough depth, or do those subjects continue across two terms?
ask.why: The term structure is WPI's most distinctive academic feature and cuts both ways.

ask.q: The Major Qualifying Project is a full-year project. Can a robotics one be done with a company or a research lab, and when do I choose it?
ask.why: The MQP is the capstone WPI is known for.

ask.q: Can I get into robotics lab space as a first-year, or is that mostly for upperclassmen?
ask.why: WPI is the only campus on your list offering prospective students lab access at all.

purdue.engineering_specific: Yes, and it maps directly onto how Purdue admits engineers. Engineering applicants enter First-Year Engineering rather than a named major - Aeronautics and Astronautics states it plainly: "There is no direct entry into the AAE program. Engineering students all start in the First-Year Engineering program." The college-level product is the Engineering Information Session (EIS) at West Lafayette, weekdays 11:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m. ET, which "includes a walking tour of our engineering facilities led by current engineering students (based on student availability)." The EIS is designed to be stacked onto a Daily Visit, and the 2021-vintage Daily Visit page confirms "EIS programs begin at 11:30 a.m." As of retrieval, Fall 2026 EIS dates were still being posted ("These events for Spring 2026 have concluded. Fall 2026 dates and registration will open in the coming months"), so the drop-in alternative matters: the Office of Future Engineers takes drop-ins Mon-Fri 9-5 in Dudley Hall with no registration. Purdue Polytechnic Institute is a distinct college with its own visit - "Discovering Purdue Polytechnic - Info Session and Tour" in Young, Dudley and Knoy Halls, with school-specific tours available (including the School of Engineering Technology); its days and times are NOT PUBLISHED. Department options add depth: ME drop-ins Mon-Fri 8:30-5 plus 3 p.m. Thursday student-led tours; BME tours Mon-Fri 1:30 p.m., no appointment; AAE by request with 4-5 business days' notice; Computer Science uses its own separate sign-up.
purdue.robotics_lab_access: NOT PUBLISHED as a standalone robotics-lab tour. The closest published access is through engineering facility walks: the EIS "includes a walking tour of our engineering facilities led by current engineering students (based on student availability)", Mechanical Engineering's 3 p.m. Thursday student-led tours, and the Polytechnic school-specific tours (School of Engineering Technology). No first-party page was found offering a dedicated robotics lab, makerspace or competition-team space tour to prospective students.
purdue.class_visit_possible: NOT PUBLISHED. No first-party Purdue admissions page found offering prospective-student class sit-ins. The realistic substitutes are the departmental drop-in advising hours (Office of Future Engineers, Mon-Fri 9-5, Dudley Hall; ME 2137 Mon-Fri 8:30-5) and department tours. If a class visit is wanted, request it directly from the department alongside a tour booking (AAE, for example, takes visit requests with 4-5 business days' notice).

read_first.q: Do I apply straight into Electrical and Computer Engineering?
read_first.a: No. You are admitted to the College of Engineering — about a 46% admit rate — and enter First-Year Engineering rather than a named major. You then request your major through the Transition to Major process after completing First-Year Engineering requirements.

read_first.q: Is Purdue's robotics degree an engineering degree?
read_first.a: Not in the strict sense. The Robotics Engineering Technology BS sits in Purdue Polytechnic and is accredited as engineering technology rather than engineering. Purdue's College of Engineering degrees, including ECE, are accredited as engineering.

ask.q: I would be admitted into First-Year Engineering rather than into a major. What does Transition to Major actually require to get into Electrical and Computer Engineering — is there a GPA number, and is ECE one of the oversubscribed ones?
ask.why: No minimum GPA for ECE is published anywhere, and this is the real gate at Purdue.

ask.q: If Transition to Major does not give me my first choice, what actually happens — do I get a second-choice major straight away, or do I wait another year?
ask.why: The downside case matters more than the upside case here.

ask.q: You publish Computer Science at about 36% and the College of Engineering at about 46%. If I want robotics and artificial intelligence, is there any real disadvantage to coming through engineering rather than computer science?
ask.why: Purdue is one of only three schools that publish rates by college, so this comparison is real.

ask.q: Purdue Polytechnic has a Robotics Engineering Technology degree and the College of Engineering has ECE. Can you explain the difference in plain terms, and which one engineering employers and graduate schools treat as an engineering degree?
ask.why: The two look interchangeable from outside and are not.

ask.q: Your Common Data Set says level of applicant's interest is considered. Does today's visit get recorded against my application?
ask.why: Purdue may count the visit, but says nothing about it in prose.

travel.suggested_stay: 2 nights - the general 90-minute Visitor Center tour and a separately-booked engineering informational are unlikely to land on the same morning, and the travel distance leaves no margin for a same-day turnaround
travel.pair_with: UT Austin - College Station to Austin is about 106 road miles, roughly 1 hour 50 minutes to 2 hours by car (routing computation), so a single Texas trip covering both is clearly the right structure. Both schools share the 1 December deadline with no early plan, so the trip can be scheduled as late as mid-November - but avoid the week of 23-27 November (A&M Thanksgiving closures, UT Austin's 23-28 November break, and the Fri 27 Nov A&M-Texas game in College Station).

texas-am.cost_notes: Tours and informationals are free. Visitor parking is paid: for the Zachry Engineering Education Complex, visitors use the Northside Garage, Central Campus Garage or Lot 51. Registration is free but required at least three days ahead. RELLIS tours are free but require a group of at least 10.

read_first.q: Do I apply to Electrical and Computer Engineering?
read_first.a: No. Engineering applicants are admitted into a common General Engineering first year, then compete for their major through Entry to a Major, known as ETAM, after at least two semesters.

ask.q: I would start in General Engineering and then go through Entry to a Major. You publish that a 3.75 cumulative GPA gets automatic entry to your first choice. If I am below 3.75, how competitive is Electrical and Computer Engineering specifically, and what have recent cut-offs looked like?
ask.why: Everything below the automatic threshold is a competition A&M does not publish numbers for.

ask.q: If Entry to a Major does not give me Electrical and Computer Engineering, what are my realistic options — do I get a second-choice major automatically, or can I be left without an engineering major at all?
ask.why: This is the single biggest risk in applying to A&M engineering.

ask.q: You have a Mechatronics degree called MXET, which I understand is engineering technology rather than engineering. If robotics is my goal, would you steer me to MXET or to Electrical and Computer Engineering, and why?
ask.why: MXET is the obvious robotics-sounding option and carries a different accreditation.

ask.q: There is no early application plan here — everything is due 1 December. Does applying earlier in the autumn make any difference to admission or to scholarships?
ask.why: Worth knowing since this trip happens after the November deadlines elsewhere.

ask.q: Your Common Data Set lists level of applicant's interest as considered. Does this visit count, and does the separately booked engineering session count as well?
ask.why: A&M's engineering visit is booked in a different system, so it may register differently.

interest.quote: No, UT Austin does not utilize demonstrated interest in the holistic review process.

ut-austin.engineering_specific: Yes - a separate Cockrell School session, and it is the highest-value item on this campus because UT admits directly to major. The Cockrell School runs its own Undergraduate Info Sessions in the Engineering Education and Research Center (EER), where advisors cover all 11 engineering majors; "attendees are welcome to take a self-guided tour through the Engineering Education and Research Center (EER)." It is booked through its own Slate portal, separate from the general campus tour. Status as of 19 August 2026: Fall 2026 in-person sessions are NOT PUBLISHED - the Cockrell page says "Fall 2026 Session Schedule: Registration and information for Fall 2026 Info Sessions opens soon," and a screenshot of the in-person engineering portal showed August 2026 with no available (burnt-orange) dates. A virtual engineering session portal exists as a fallback. Because UT locks you into a major at admission and does not offer class visits in engineering, the Cockrell session plus the Texas Robotics AHG tour is the combination that actually answers the applicant's robotics/AI questions - the general 2-hour campus tour will not.
ut-austin.robotics_lab_access: Yes, and it is the strongest robotics access in this batch after Michigan. Texas Robotics offers registered tours of Anna Hiss Gymnasium (2501 Wichita St): "We welcome visitors to explore Anna Hiss Gymnasium, home of Texas Robotics at The University of Texas at Austin," booked through the "Schedule a Tour" link on https://robotics.utexas.edu/visit. Expect scarcity and no published schedule: "availability is limited since these tours are offered in addition to their primary responsibilities," and "Anna Hiss Gymnasium is an active academic and research facility, not a museum." Days, times and lead time are NOT PUBLISHED, so email robotics@utexas.edu / submit the scheduling form well before the trip. Secondary access: the self-guided walk through the EER building offered to Cockrell info-session attendees.
ut-austin.class_visit_possible: No, not in engineering - Cockrell states it plainly: "Because we want to maintain the integrity of our classes for our current students, the Cockrell School does not offer classroom visits, but we encourage you to attend one of our special programs for admitted students." The substitutes are the Cockrell info session with advisors, the self-guided EER walk, and the Texas Robotics AHG tour.

read_first.a: No. UT states it plainly: "UT Austin does not utilize demonstrated interest in the holistic review process." Visit to decide, not to be counted.

read_first.q: Can I sit in on an engineering class?
read_first.a: No — the Cockrell School does not allow classroom visits.

ask.q: You admit students directly to a major. If I apply to Electrical and Computer Engineering and am not admitted, am I considered for anything else, or is it simply a no?
ask.why: Direct-to-major admission means a rejected first choice may end the application entirely.

ask.q: Computer Science sits in a different college here from engineering. Can I apply to both Electrical and Computer Engineering and Computer Science, or do I have to pick one?
ask.why: The two live in different colleges, so the rules are not obvious.

ask.q: How hard is it to switch into Computer Science after I arrive, if I decide I want more software than hardware?
ask.why: Internal transfer into CS is described as restricted, so the real difficulty matters.

ask.q: Once I am in Electrical and Computer Engineering, is there any GPA requirement to stay in it, or to get the technical area I want when I choose at the end of second year?
ask.why: UT appears to have no gate once admitted — worth confirming, because that is unusual.

ask.q: Texas Robotics is based in the Anna Hiss Gymnasium. Can undergraduates work in those labs, and starting from which year?
ask.why: Undergraduate lab access is the main thing a website will not tell you.

dont_ask.q: Does showing interest or visiting improve my chances?
dont_ask.because: UT Austin states it does not use demonstrated interest at all.
